collection_method: Read-only global GitHub issue search followed by full review of the public upstream issue, pull-request metadata and patch. Embedded code and tests were treated as evidence and were not executed; no package, agent runtime, attachment or target system was opened or run.
searches: wrong agent plus executed, created from 2026-10-05
agent plus wrong recipient, created from 2026-10-05

selected_records.title: Team wakeups cross namespace boundaries for same-named members
selected_records.verified_participants: controlled test roles in two intentionally configured namespaces, with distinct bound session identifiers; no independent autonomous model identities are authenticated
selected_records.task_result_transfer_observed: the unfixed bridge can route message notices and task completion or failure text from namespace A to the same-named member session in namespace B
selected_records.recipient_use_observed: not established; tests inspect the wrong inbox and wakeup queue, but do not run the recipient model or show the foreign result changing its work
selected_records.operator_boundary_crossed: the controlled reproduction violates the framework's namespace-isolation contract and can wake the wrong session while leaving the intended recipient idle
selected_records.provider_attribution: AgentScope Java Harness routing defect; no inference-model or hosted-provider execution is shown
selected_records.ongoing_activity: the issue and patch remained open when observed; this establishes current project remediation, not ongoing affected agent activity
selected_records.assessment: A fresh, high-quality wrong-recipient transfer control with a concrete isolation boundary. It is a deterministic framework test in a deliberately configured team, not a real autonomous exchange or rogue swarm.

selected_records.title: Fix: isolate team wakeups by namespace
selected_records.assessment: The patch and regression tests corroborate the mechanism: namespace was discarded at the wakeup bridge and registrations were keyed only by team and member names. The tests cover message, assignment and completion/failure notices, but remain controlled transport-level evidence.

novelty_result: No previously unreported rogue swarm confirmed. The record was newly collected by this project but had already been published upstream on 5 October 2026.
limitations: The public evidence is a reporter-authored issue, patch and controlled regression suite rather than a production incident transcript or provider postmortem.
Receipt in a wrong session inbox and wakeup queue does not prove that an autonomous recipient read or used the transferred text.
Configured team members and sessions do not independently authenticate distinct autonomous agents.
Open issue or pull-request status does not establish that affected software was deployed or that the behavior remains active in any agent system.
The global lexical searches are bounded discovery passes with overlapping results, not a census of GitHub issues.
redactions: No raw task text beyond generic test labels, private logs, local paths, credentials, tokens or runtime identifiers are reproduced.
Only canonical public links, dates, hashes, public commit identifiers and domain-level behavior summaries are retained.
